task.name: Sprint re-exec drops its own preflighted story as a worktree collision and books the drop as unbounded unmeasured spend, halting the rest of the sprint
task.story_text:
## Observed

Sprint `issues-2976,2860,2651,2652,2503,1759,2980,2596,2914,2951,2947,2948,2985,1802` (sprint id `db3d1526dcbc`, run `f7bd26b82e60`, v0.16.0rc19, `--budget 300 --parallel 2`, 2026-09-12) started 08:24 PT. Story issue-2951 already had a worktree carrying 3 commits from an earlier sprint (2026-09-08). At launch this sprint reattached that worktree and ran preflight on the story (08:22, `↻ WORKSPACE branch has commits, reattaching worktree: feat/issue-2951`) but had not yet dispatched it.

After issue-1759 landed, the sprint re-exec'd mid-run (09:36). The re-exec'd process logged issue-1802 and issue-2503 as IN-FLIGHT and preserved them, but reported:

```
[forge] DROPPED issue-2951: active worktree collision after re-exec; continuing with remaining stories.
[sprint] 09:45:04.689 DROPPED issue-2951 (reason: active-worktree-collision: 3 unmerged commit(s) on branch feat/issue-2951, preserved at .forge/worktrees/issue-2951)
```

The drop was then recorded as an unmeasured spend source with no ceiling, and every remaining story was skipped on it, including the two the log had just called in-flight:

```
[sprint] 09:45:08.138 SKIPPED issue-1802 (budget unverifiable (spend unmeasured for 1 source(s) [dropped-with-work:issue-2951]; measured $19.32 of $300.00 cap is a lower bound, so the cap cannot be verified; unresolved: dropped-with-work:issue-2951: unbounded (no per-story audit found for this source; origin not recorded)))
[sprint] 09:45:13.368 Sprint complete: 1 succeeded, 1 failed, 12 skipped. Total: unknown (>= $19.32 measured)
```

`--accept-unmeasured-spend dropped-with-work:issue-2951` offers no way out: the source has no derivable ceiling, so the acceptance is refused and the guard stays closed. No agent spend occurred on issue-2951 in this sprint. After the halt, issue-1802's worktree no longer exists although it was reported in-flight; issue-2503's worktree holds a `wip: uncommitted changes from dev iteration 1` commit.

Artifacts: `.forge/logs/issues-2976,2860,2651,2652,2503,1759,2980,2596,2914,2951,2947,2948,2985,1802/run-f7bd26b82e60.log`, `sprint-summary.yaml`, `.forge/sprints/db3d1526dcbc/state.yaml`.

## Expected

A story that belongs to the sprint's own story list is the sprint's own work on every generation of that sprint, whether or not it had been dispatched when a re-exec fired, so a re-exec never reclassifies it as a foreign collision. Work a sprint did not spend money on in this sprint is never booked as unmeasured spend of that sprint. When a budget guard does close on an unknown, the halt names a recovery the operator can actually take, and a single unknown attributable to one story does not silently discard the rest of the sprint at a fraction of its cap.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `db41edf2307370c27f424325a0134a9139985a72` captured at `2026-09-13T19:27:10.889968+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

### Observed symptom

A story that belongs to the sprint's own manifest, and whose worktree the
sprint itself reattached at launch, is reclassified as a foreign
"active-worktree-collision" and dropped the moment the sprint re-execs
mid-run before that story was ever dispatched to a worker. The drop is then
booked as an unbounded "unmeasured spend" source (no agent ever ran on the
story in this sprint, so there is no per-story audit to derive a ceiling
from), and because the sprint-wide budget cap can no longer be verified
against an unbounded unknown, every remaining story — including two the same
log had just called IN-FLIGHT — is SKIPPED, halting a 14-story, $300 sprint
at $19.32 of measured spend with 12 stories never run. The documented
recovery path, `--accept-unmeasured-spend`, is refused for this specific
source because it has no derivable ceiling to charge.

### Reproduction / evidence

Run log
`.forge/logs/issues-2976,2860,2651,2652,2503,1759,2980,2596,2914,2951,2947,2948,2985,1802/run-f7bd26b82e60.log`
and sprint state `.forge/sprints/db3d1526dcbc/state.yaml`, sprint
`db3d1526dcbc` / run `f7bd26b82e60`:
- 08:22:20 — WORKSPACE reattaches issue-2951's pre-existing worktree
  (`↻ WORKSPACE branch has commits, reattaching worktree: feat/issue-2951`),
  a worktree carrying 3 commits from an earlier, unrelated sprint
  (2026-09-08).
- 08:24:41 — DAG/routing bookkeeping for issue-2951 runs (worker timeout
  derivation, collision-injected `depends_on issue-2948`), but no
  WORKSPACE→PLAN/DEV dispatch line for issue-2951 ever appears before the
  re-exec: it is queued behind sibling stories the whole first generation.
- 09:35:53 — sprint re-execs after issue-1802 pulls new source.
- 09:36:41 — launch guard re-exec path prints
  `[forge] DROPPED issue-2951: active worktree collision after re-exec;
  continuing with remaining stories.` while, on the same launch, issue-1802
  and issue-2503 (which *had* been dispatched) are recognized as
  `IN-FLIGHT ... this sprint dispatched the story and has not settled it`.
- 09:45:04.689 — the scheduler reaches issue-2951's DAG slot and finalizes
  the drop: `DROPPED issue-2951 (reason: active-worktree-collision: 3
  unmerged commit(s) on branch feat/issue-2951, preserved at
  .forge/worktrees/issue-2951)`, and `.forge/sprints/db3d1526dcbc/state.yaml`
  records `slug: issue-2951 / outcome: DROPPED / cost_usd: null / drop_reason:
  active-worktree-collision`.
- 09:45:08 onward — every remaining story is SKIPPED with `budget
  unverifiable ... unresolved: dropped-with-work:issue-2951: unbounded (no
  per-story audit found for this source; origin not recorded)`.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** The re-exec launch guard's foreign-collision classification (launch_guard.py's `acquire_launch_story_locks`, allow_drop path) has no way to recognize a sprint's own not-yet-dispatched story as its own work, because its two 'this is mine' tests — live/registered in-flight status (`live_slugs`/`registered_slugs`, sourced from `story_executions.register_story_execution`, written only 'before a story is dispatched') and a prior-generation outcome record (from `_resolve_prior_outcomes` → `_load_accumulated_stories`) — both require the story to have already been handed to a worker at least once in this sprint. A story still queued behind DAG dependencies when the re-exec fires has neither, so it falls through to the generic `REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE` branch even though the worktree's commits were knowingly reattached by this same sprint's own launch moments earlier.
  - Evidence: Read launch_guard.py lines 156-174 (confirmed_live/unresolved_live derived only from live_slugs/unresolved_slugs/registered_slugs) and lines 292-313 (the active_worktrees loop: reconciled only if reconcilable_prior_success(prior_raw), stranded if any prior_outcome exists, else REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE). Read story_executions.py's module docstring and register_story_execution docstring, both stating registration happens only 'before a story is dispatched.' Read cli/sprint.py `_resolve_prior_outcomes`, which reads only `_load_accumulated_stories` (records a generation actually wrote). Cross- checked the run log: issue-2951 shows WORKSPACE-reattach and DAG/routing bookkeeping at 08:22-08:24 but no PLAN/DEV dispatch line before the 09:35 re-exec — it never reached the point where `register_story_execution` is called (that call site is only reached at actual dispatch, per grep of runner.py around line 4093-4100) — and state.yaml shows no accumulated entry for it from generation 1.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Verified directly against launch_guard.py, story_executions.py, cli/sprint.py source at HEAD, cross-referenced against the attached run log and sprint state.yaml.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Traced the actual code paths and matched them against the timestamped log lines and state.yaml entry for issue-2951; not a restatement of a prior assertion.
- **[confirmed]** The drop-handling code in runner.py treats any worktree with non-base commits as proof that 'this run' spent money on it, and when it cannot find a same-sprint prior-generation audit to attribute that spend to, flags the drop as an unbounded unmeasured-spend source — which is correct for a story this sprint actually dispatched and lost track of across a re-exec, but wrong for a story whose commits predate this sprint entirely and that this sprint never dispatched at all.
  - Evidence: Read runner.py lines 6964-7003: the comment states 'if its worktree holds commits, it did run ... the spend was the previous process image's, so it is recovered from the audit that generation flushed ... and recorded as unmeasured — never as zero — when there is not.' `_attribute_prior_generation_cost` (lines 6793-6833) only recovers cost from `_sprint_state.prior_generation_work`, populated for stories that were in flight when a re-exec boundary was crossed — which issue-2951, never dispatched, cannot be. `work_detail` is still truthy because `_inspect_dropped_work`/`describe_worktree_work` only inspects git history ahead of base, with no check for whether *this sprint* produced those commits. This lines up exactly with the log's `dropped-with-work:issue-2951: unbounded (no per-story audit found for this source; origin not recorded)`.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Verified directly against runner.py source at HEAD and matched against the run log's unmeasured-spend message text.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Traced the code path producing the exact unresolved-source string seen in the log; independent of any prior diagnosis.
- **[ruled out]** The reuse-gate/triage classification ('DEV (worktree exists, gate fails ...)' at 09:39:14) is what actually caused the final drop, rather than the launch guard's earlier classification.
  - Evidence: The 09:39:14 triage line comes from a separate, purely informational per-slug loop (`_log('Triaging specs...')` at runner.py:5970, iterating `_ctx.slug_to_context` and calling `_triage_spec` for every non-in-flight slug) that populates a `triages` dict and does not consult or override `dropped_slugs` from the launch guard. The actual drop-with-audit line at 09:45:04 uses the `active-worktree-collision` reason string and the exact 3-unmerged-commit/worktree-path detail that only the launch guard's `REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE` branch (launch_guard.py:312, computed at 09:36:41 launch) produces; the DAG simply deferred processing that already-dropped slug until 09:45 because of its collision-injected `depends_on` chain.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Checked directly against runner.py's triage loop and the drop- processing block, and against the DAG dependency lines logged at 08:24:41 for issue-2951.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Independently traced by reading the two code paths and ordering them against the timestamps in the log.

### Confirmed cause

On a mid-run re-exec, the sprint's launch guard
(`acquire_launch_story_locks` in `src/theforge/sprint/launch_guard.py`,
re-exec/`allow_drop` branch) classifies a story's own worktree as a foreign
`active-worktree-collision` (`REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE`) whenever the story has
not yet been dispatched to a worker in this sprint — because the guard's
only two "this is my own work" tests (a live/registered in-flight record
from `story_executions`, written only at dispatch time; or a prior-
generation outcome record from `_resolve_prior_outcomes`, written only once
a generation has produced a story entry) both require a dispatch that has
not yet happened. A story that the sprint itself reattached and DAG-
scheduled at launch, but that is still queued behind `depends_on` when the
re-exec fires, has neither signal and is misclassified as foreign. The
resulting drop is then processed by the runner's drop-with-work accounting
(`src/theforge/sprint/runner.py`, the `else` branch following the
`_stranded_prior` check, roughly lines 6964-7003): finding non-base commits
on the worktree, it treats that as proof this sprint spent money running the
story, and — finding no `prior_generation_work` entry to attribute that
spend to, because this sprint never actually dispatched it —
`flag_unmeasured_here(f"dropped-with-work:{slug}")` records the drop as an
unbounded unmeasured-spend source. That unbounded, un-originated source then
fails the sprint-wide budget verification for every remaining story.

Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Both halves of the causal chain were verified by reading the current HEAD of launch_guard.py, story_executions.py, cli/sprint.py, and runner.py, then cross-checked line-by-line against the timestamped run log and sprint state.yaml attached to the issue.
Support: Direct reading of `launch_guard.py`'s re-exec branch (lines 275-337) shows
the three-way classification (`RECONCILE_PRIOR_DONE` / `STRANDED_WORKTREE` /
`ACTIVE_WORKTREE`) is driven entirely by `prior_outcomes.get(slug)`, itself
sourced from `_resolve_prior_outcomes` → `_load_accumulated_stories`
(`cli/sprint.py`), which only contains entries a generation actually wrote.
`story_executions.py`'s own module docstring documents that ownership
records exist specifically to prevent this exact failure mode for stories a
sprint *did* dispatch (citing #2617) but are, by the docstring's own
description, written only "before a story is dispatched" — leaving a
never-dispatched, DAG-queued story with no record at all. The run log
independently confirms issue-2951 was never dispatched in the first
generation (WORKSPACE reattach and DAG bookkeeping only, no PLAN/DEV line)
before the 09:35:53 re-exec, and `state.yaml` records `cost_usd: null` for
its DROPPED entry — consistent with zero spend, not with lost-but-real
spend.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. The mechanism was traced directly from source; the log/state.yaml citations are primary run artifacts, not restatements of a prior diagnosis (the issue body's own 'Diagnosis' section was empty, status 'no diagnosis yet').
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/sprint/launch_guard.py:292-313 (acquire_launch_story_locks,
re-exec active-worktree classification — REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE fallback for
a story with no live/registered in-flight record and no prior-generation
outcome); src/theforge/sprint/story_executions.py (register_story_execution
is written only at dispatch time, leaving a DAG-queued-but-undispatched
story with no ownership record at re-exec); src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:500-535
(_resolve_prior_outcomes / _load_accumulated_stories, the source of
prior_outcomes consulted by the guard); src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:6964-6994
(the drop-with-work branch that flags an unbounded
dropped-with-work:<slug> unmeasured-spend source whenever a dropped story's
worktree has non-base commits but no prior_generation_work entry exists to
attribute cost to).

### Fix-success criterion

Re-running an equivalent scenario — a sprint story whose worktree the sprint
itself reattached/prepared at launch but that had not yet been dispatched to
a worker when a mid-run re-exec fires — must NOT be dropped as
active-worktree-collision, must not appear as an unmeasured-spend source in
the resumed run, and the remaining sibling stories must continue to be
scheduled up to the budget cap rather than being universally SKIPPED for an
unverifiable budget.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- launch_guard.py's re-exec collision branch prints '... continuing with remaining stories' immediately followed by calling abort_for_active_worktrees(collision_slugs), whose 'Aborting' message is printed but whose return value is discarded — a confusing but functionally inert contradiction in the log output.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Two independent, composable fixes suggest themselves (not verified as
sufficient on their own): (1) in launch_guard.py's re-exec branch, treat
simple membership in the sprint's own `slugs`/DAG with no prior-generation
outcome record as "this sprint's own not-yet-dispatched work" rather than a
collision by default — the ownership registry and prior-outcome record are
sufficient-but-not-necessary evidence of ownership, not the only possible
evidence, since a story that was merely reattached/DAG-scheduled by this
same sprint (never a foreign process) should not need either signal to be
recognized as this sprint's own. (2) In runner.py's drop-with-work
accounting, only flag `dropped-with-work` unmeasured spend when there is
positive evidence this sprint (any of its generations) actually dispatched
the story — e.g. an ownership record, a prior_generation_work entry, or a
DAG dispatch log entry — rather than inferring "it did run" purely from the
worktree having non-base commits, since those commits can predate the
sprint entirely (as here, from an unrelated sprint on 2026-09-08). Separately,
the halt-message/escape-hatch gap ("a single unknown ... discards the rest
of the sprint" and "the halt names a recovery the operator can actually
take") may need its own remediation in the unmeasured-spend guard
(src/theforge/sprint/unmeasured.py) even after the misclassification itself
is fixed, e.g. by not letting one attributable-to-one-story unknown gate
unrelated stories, or by letting `--accept-unmeasured-spend` accept a
zero-ceiling source when there is affirmative evidence (like this case) that
the source is a misclassification rather than lost spend.

### Notes

A secondary, cosmetic-only defect: in launch_guard.py's re-exec branch, when
`collision_slugs` is non-empty it prints "DROPPED ...: continuing with
remaining stories" immediately followed by a call to
`abort_for_active_worktrees(collision_slugs)` whose return value is
discarded — that function prints "Stories already have active worktrees:
...  Aborting." even though nothing is aborted here. This produced the
contradictory log pair at 09:36:41 ("continuing" then "Aborting") but does
not itself change scheduling behavior (dropped_slugs already recorded, and
the discarded exit code has no effect), so it is not part of the confirmed
cause — flagging it only because it made the log confusing to read during
this investigation.

I did not attempt to reproduce this live (no forge sprint launch was run);
the diagnosis rests on direct source reading cross-checked line-by-line
against the attached run log and sprint state.yaml, which is a strong but
not experimentally-reproduced form of confirmation.
## Impact

A multi-story sprint on the dogfood substrate halts at $19 of a $300 cap with 12 of 14 stories never run, whenever any listed story has a worktree from an earlier generation and the sprint re-execs after a landing. The operator's documented escape hatch for an unmeasured-spend halt refuses this source by construction.

finding_registry.description: The re-exec pending-story preservation is asserted at the launch-guard boundary (the story is absent from dropped and holds a lock) and the spend-evidence gating is asserted at the runner boundary, but no test drives the two together, so nothing verifies that a story the guard now leaves schedulable is actually dispatched by the scheduler in a resumed run rather than being re-dropped or skipped downstream.

When a re-exec cannot resolve prior outcomes, the CLI can pass an empty prior-outcome map and an active selected worktree with no prior record is kept schedulable instead of being dropped as a collision.

When a re-exec's prior-generation state cannot actually be read — a truncated or malformed state.yaml, or a sprint-id lookup that fell back to a freshly minted id whose state directory does not exist — the prior outcome resolution still reports a successfully resolved empty mapping, so the launch guard treats every selected story with an active worktree as this sprint's own pending work and keeps it schedulable.

On a sprint's first generation the re-exec that fires while pulling the base branch happens before any story has settled, so the sprint's accumulated state file does not exist yet, and the re-exec'd launch treats that absence as an unresolvable ownership lookup and drops every listed story whose worktree carries commits from an earlier sprint as a foreign active-worktree collision.

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
